utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, if there is nothing else, then we'll have the next witness. Who is dealing with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It's me, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Are there any protective measures for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, there are. He requested image distortion, but he does not need a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's very strange. Does the witness fully understand the purpose for the protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We explained it to him yesterday and he said he's fine to testify under his real name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, you may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Waespi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Waespi:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember that we met yesterday in my office?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that we advised you of your right to remain silent and to have a lawyer present if you wanted. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you waived these rights and said that you were fine with discussing your evidence without the presence of a lawyer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also told us yesterday that you would be willing to testify today under the same conditions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So today you're ready to proceed and answer questions without the presence of a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also told us that you requested image distortion and we have been told by the Court that this would be granted. Now you said you were fine that your full name appears. Is that correct? Are you fine with your name becoming public?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm fine with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. So can you please state for the record your full name.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Cvijetin Ristanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please spell out your last name, please.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: R-i-s-t-a-n-o-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were you born?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 15th of April, 1949.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: In Kostijerovo village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which municipality would that be?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what's your profession and are you currently working somewhere?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I am an operator of construction machines and I'm currently employed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where are you employed?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The 6th Oktobar Colopek Zvornik private company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now did you serve in the JNA at one time?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: That was between 1968 and 1970.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the war, and I mean the war between 1992 and 1995, did you serve in the army as well?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which unit did you serve?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the engineering unit of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from when to when did you serve in the engineering unit?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date, but I believe that it was July 1992 and March -- the beginning of March or the end of February 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your rank?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe briefly your duties.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. My duties since I was in the engineering unit in the unit that was in charge for the reparation of roads, building bridges in villages, everything that had to do with the infrastructure, the road infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in June 1995, do you remember what you were doing in that month?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: June, in June I was -- at the beginning of the month I was in my unit and then I went to Nisici to the separation line and that's where I manned the line together with others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do afterwards, after you returned from the Nisici area?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, when I returned from Nisici, I was given some time off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how many days that was?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I believe it was six, seven, or eight days. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, with your permission, Your Honours, I would like to show the first exhibit to this witness and this would be 514, Zvornik Brigade engineering brigade attendance roster for the month of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look at the first page and then flip over to the last page. Now if you look at number 9 on the last page, do you see your name written there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you continue along the line to the right, what's written there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It says the 1st, the 2nd, the 3rd up to the 4th Nisici, the 5th and the 6th as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that will be reference to your assignment at Nisici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we have a few C's what could that mean?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It may be either a C or an S, I don't know, but I believe that means days off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we have a cross on the 14th. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that could be an indication that this was your first day at work again?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Probably, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If we could return this exhibit. Now, do you remember the first day you came back from leave?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly whether I returned on the 13th or on the 14th. I can't remember the date exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you go to work the next day after you returned?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at what time in the morning would you do that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It depended on my orders. My orders sometimes didn't arrive in the morning; sometimes they arrived in the afternoon or at any point in time during the course of the day. It varied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on that day do you remember when you showed up at work?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I came to work at 7.00 in the morning. I was present in the unit like every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us where that unit was, where did you report to work?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The unit was in the Karakaj Omladinsko Naselje in the youth settlement. That was the headquarters of the engineering unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now in relation to Zvornik, the town centre of Zvornik, how far away would that be?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It may be 4 kilometres, maybe more maybe less, but I would say about 4 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it north or south of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It would be on the north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the road between Zvornik and Bijeljina, how far away from the road Zvornik Bijeljina in Karakaj would the engineering unit be located?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The Bijeljina/Zvornik road, maybe 300, 400, or 500 metres. I can't tell you exactly. Anything between 300 and 500 metres, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was there a factory as well in that area where the company was located?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, across the road there was the Birac clay factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who was your company commander?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: My company commander was Dragan Jevtic. There were other people as well, but at that time it was Dragan Jevtic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you part of a platoon?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did it have a commander, your platoon, and if so, what was his name?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. His name was Damjan Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your platoon, what was the name of it?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It was road platoon, Putni platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you came into work on that day, did you receive an order from somebody?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Not in the morning, but it was before noon. I don't know exactly when. I did receive my orders, but that was not early in the morning. It was before noon, however.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who gave you this order?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the chief of engineers, Dragan Jokic came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Dragan Jokic well?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since when did you know him?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: From 1992; I don't know from which month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you receive often orders from him?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes from him, sometimes from the company commander, sometimes from the platoon commander. I don't remember whether this happened often or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what was the order Mr. Jokic gave you on that morning before noon?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: When he came, he said that I and my machine were to go to Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us where Orahovac is located?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you tell you were in Orahovac you would have to go to?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I believe that he said school, the school in Orahovac or thereabouts. I can't remember exactly. I can't really quote what the order was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you told what to do there by Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who else, if anybody, was present when you were receiving this order?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was the lorry driver who transported a piece of equipment. There was another soldier, Risto Lazic, and I believe that Slavko Bogicevic was also present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is Slavko Bogicevic?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Bogicevic, he was the company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought earlier you had said that Mr. Jevtic was the company commander. Can you clarify that to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I said that Slavko Bogicevic was in the command of the company. He was not the commander, but he was one of the command staff of the company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the driver of the truck, what was his name?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: His name was Milan Maksimovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what machinery did you take with you?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: A G-700, that was the piece of equipment that I took with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe it to the Trial Chamber, how this piece of machinery looked like.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a piece of equipment which has an excavating -- a hydraulic piece of equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was it used for?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It is used for excavations, road excavations, canal excavations. It is used for excavations and for loading the earth that is excavated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who owned this piece of equipment?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the owner was Zvornik Putevi, a company based in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that morning when you took this machinery, where was it located, inside or outside the compound of the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It was within the compound of the engineering company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could please be shown the next exhibit, and this is an exhibit which Your Honours have received from the head of interpretation unit. And perhaps if we have a copy that could be put on to the ELMO. Mr. Ristanovic, can you tell us whether you see this G-700, as explained by you, on this sketch, and if so, which one would it be. It doesn't need to be accurate, but perhaps you can see something which is close to what you took to Orahovac on that day.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're pointing to the one in the top row, the one in the middle, called backhoe excavator, and I think there is a note, Rovokopac in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, people call it different names. Some people call it backhoe excavator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could return this exhibit and go to the next one. And this would be P62. Can you tell us, Mr. Ristanovic, what this machinery is, is that something similar?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's called BGH-600, and I understand there also -- there is a model BGH-700. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what the difference would be.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The difference is in the make or the producer. The BGH-600 is smaller. It is a smaller backhoe loader. It has a smaller grab. It can only contain 0.60 cubic metres, so that is the only difference, in the size of the front grab. So it is the name, the make, the producer, it depends on who the manufacturer of the machinery is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If we could take that away. Now, on that day I understand you didn't drive this vehicle to Orahovac but it was loaded on to another vehicle. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Which vehicle are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The G-700.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I loaded that piece of equipment on to a truck, and that is the piece of equipment that I worked with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how long did it take for you to load this machinery on to the trailer?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: We never timed it. It all depends. Sometimes it takes 20 minutes, sometimes it takes half an hour, sometimes it takes even more. It all depends on the place where you do the loading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you do the loading that morning?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: At the headquarters of the engineering company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, which route did you take to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: From the headquarters, we came to the road leading to Zvornik. We arrived that -- the crossroads in Karakaj, and then we continued on the road towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did the trip take in time?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I don't know. I don't know how long it took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us a distance in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean from the headquarters to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, perhaps 15 to 20 kilometres, something like that. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you were driving towards Tuzla. Now, I understand you didn't go to Tuzla but at that time you took a different route. Can you indicate which one that would be?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we came to the village of Orahovac, we turned off to Krizevici. We continued along the road there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you had to go to the school at Orahovac. Now, did you go to the school at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That road goes by the school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you stop at the school in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: When we reached the school, I think there were some trucks there on the road trying to turn around as far as I can remember that. So that's how we had to stay there, we couldn't pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of trucks were they, civilian, or military?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I think they were civilian trucks, I think so. I think they were civilian trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you see soldiers present in that area where you had to stop?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were these soldiers? Were they from a specific unit? Did you recognise any insignia or anything else which would indicate to you where they were from?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they had camouflage uniforms on and I think I saw military policemen there, too, members of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of which brigade these military police were from?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how many policemen did you see there, military policemen?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't count them. I noticed that there were some of them there, but I can't say exactly. I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for how long did you stop at that school?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly now, perhaps four or five minutes until we were able to pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: We went on further. We continued our journey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how long did you continue your journey?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean in terms of time or in terms of the number of kilometres?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number of kilometres.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps another 500 to 600 metres or up to 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: When we got there, somebody stopped us there and told us to stop there and wait.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who told you to stop and wait?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember, perhaps the driver knows. I really cannot remember who told us to wait there once we stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you stopped -- that location, what was that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: We stopped on the road between Orahovac and Krizevici there are meadows on both sides, and there's water there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say there was water there, what was it, a source, a water point, a pump?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: There was a water point there, perhaps there is a source there and the water was tapped from that source or perhaps there was just a tap coming from elsewhere. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at that water point, what did you see? Did you see people there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. There were some soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many you saw there.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't -- I wasn't counting. There were soldiers there. I don't know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do next once you had arrived?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: We waited there for a while, and then somebody came and told me to unload the machine, to get this off the truck. And that's what I did. And then they told me to leave it by the water point, and there is this road that goes under the underpass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And an underpass under what?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Under the Zivinice/Zvornik railroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said somebody came to tell you to unload the truck, do you remember who that was?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember with 100 per cent certainty. When I went up there after having unloaded the things there, I saw Slavko Bogicevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you to do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: He told me to take the machine up there -- I mean after the underpass, to take it through the underpass and then to the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it difficult to manoeuvre the machine through the underpass?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why was it difficult?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It's narrow and low, so I barely managed to get through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you described earlier that on the other side there was a meadow. Can you describe a little bit more to Your Honours what you saw there.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: When I went through the underpass, I reached a meadow. There was a meadow in front of me. Behind the meadow was a forest, straight ahead if I remember exactly. On the other side, there was corn, maize, I can't remember, but I know right in front of me there was a meadow and behind the meadow was a forest. As far as I can remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before we go into what you were doing there, did you remember the time you had arrived at the water point and unloaded the machine?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I didn't have a watch or anything. I can't give you the exact time. I really don't know. I don't know. I think it was around midday or just after midday, something like that, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now at the meadow, did you see any vehicles at that time, any people around or was it empty?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was some people there at this meadow, there were some soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I was told to go towards the forest with the machine and to dig.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who told you to start to dig?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was Slavko Bogicevic who told me where -- or rather, that I was supposed to dig there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you supposed to dig?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: There were four wooden poles there, and he told me to dig right there, between these four poles, this area that had been marked in that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us the extent, the size of this area, you know, how wide it was and how long and how deep?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't measure it. I don't know. In my estimate, perhaps the width was about 2 and a half to 3 metres or between 2 and 2 and a half metres. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We just talked about how wide it was. Do you know how long it was?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't measure that either, but tentatively speaking, perhaps it was about 15 metres in length, perhaps more, perhaps less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you start to dig at one time then?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I did. I did start to dig, and I asked someone how deep I was supposed to dig. Now, I don't remember who it was that I asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you get an answer?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how deep were you told to dig?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: From a metre and a half to 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were digging, did Slavko Bogicevic stay there or did he go away? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see Slavko Bogicevic there after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you able to finish the digging, or did something happen while you were digging?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: When I started to dig, I don't know how much time I spent digging, somebody came up to me and told me to switch off the machine and to get out of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: They told me to follow them, to go back, to step back from the machine, to walk towards the underpass, towards the railroad. They showed me where I was supposed to stand. They told me to go in that direction and to stand there and to turn around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by turning around, you mean turning away from the hole you were digging?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I had my back facing that direction and I heard vehicles coming, trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many trucks was that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard the trucks coming, do you remember whether it was one truck or more?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: One truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: When the truck came there, then I heard shouts, Get out, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: And then soon afterwards, bursts of gunfire were heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long you heard these bursts of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I couldn't say how long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you -- did somebody tell you to go back?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: To continue digging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you see when you returned back to your machine?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw corpses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges how many corpses you saw at that time?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't count. I just caught a glimpse of them, and when I realised what this was, I turned my head away. I couldn't watch, so I really don't know how many there were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether these corpses of which you caught a glimpse had uniforms on or were they in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: At that first moment, I didn't see that, but later on I saw that they were wearing civilian clothes. At that first moment when I caught a glimpse of them, I was so frightened that I had to turn away, but afterwards I realised that they were wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see blindfolds?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of these blindfolds?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I think white. I don't know, I think they were white, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you continue to dig the hole?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you ordered to do that or did you just continue on on your own?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I was told to go on digging after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then who told you that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I really can't. I don't know. I don't know who told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were continuing to dig, were you again interrupted by trucks or were you able to finish digging?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that they were -- that they interrupted me once again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "they," whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean these soldiers who were there, those who were carrying out the executions. That's who I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say you were interrupted again, did the same sequence of events happen as you have just described to the Judges?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you able to finish the hole yourself, or did somebody else take over at one time?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Another machinist came to work, another machinist was sent to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us the name of this machinist?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: His name is Milovan Miladinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of which unit he was a member of?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, he was in the engineering unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember when he came, the time of the day?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean -- well, he came in the afternoon. I don't know what time it was; that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how far you were in digging the hole? Had you almost finished or were you still in the beginning?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember right now. Perhaps I had dug half of it, but I really can't remember now. It was a long time ago; it was eight years ago. I cannot remember how much I had dug by then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I understand from what you just told us that he came after certainly the first shooting you had described. Can you confirm that. Did Mr. Miladinovic arrive after you had seen that execution happening?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would have -- he would have seen the bodies around the hole?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: He could have. I think he could have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did he do when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. He arrived. He said that they had sent him there, and he took the machine and started working. I went down to the water point and I washed my face, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you who told him to come?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Miladinovic took over the machine from you, he didn't bring his own machine?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: He took it over from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you went to the water point, and I believe you washed your face?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to have a drink of water, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe us what you saw at the water point.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing. There was some soldiers there, things like that for the first moment or so. And then I saw corpses there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time did you see corpses?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was almost the end of the day, towards the end of the day. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us why these corpses were there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably the persons who were driven there and then executed there at that site, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know more about that, did you see anybody bringing these corpses, or indeed, the persons before they were executed?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: As I was there by the water point, at one moment or another, I don't know, vehicles were coming back from the direction of Baljkovica. And then this vehicle stopped there and they took a man out and shot him right there by the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away were you from the site where this person was shot?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps 20 metres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of vehicle was that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, I really don't. I don't know whether it was a small TAM truck or a passenger vehicle. I really can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that they took a man out. Can you describe the person who took the man out.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot. The man had a camouflage uniform on, but I cannot describe him because I practically didn't see him. I just know he wore a camouflage uniform, that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you described this killing. While you were there at the water point, did you witness other killings like that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I saw this same kind of thing happen there twice, as I was going there to the water point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how far away from the road were these bodies?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe 5 or 6 or 10 metres away, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, by the end of the afternoon, are you able to tell the Trial Chamber how many bodies you saw at that spot near the water point?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't count. I really don't know how many bodies there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us a rough estimate, was it 10 or was it 100?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I really didn't count them. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like you to look at a sketch. This is exhibit P661. Now, Mr. Ristanovic, do you recognise this drawing?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think we need the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this drawing as well?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I made this drawing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us the locations. If you could start with the -- what you described as skola, the way you arrived from -- the way you have arrived from the main road towards the school and then where you were digging the grave.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived from the Zvornik/Tuzla road. We forked off towards Orahovac. We passed by the school and this is where we arrived by the water point here. Here there is another road which goes under the passage. And the underpassage is here. I passed through the underpass. This is the meadow and this is the forest and this is where I dug out this grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you can again go to the right part where the meadow was and I think you indicated where grave number 1 was, the grave you had started to dig first. Can you indicate that again.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: This is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us where you were standing when the first execution was underway. You told the Trial Chamber that you had to go away towards the railway. Did you indicate on that sketch where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Here. Here, I was standing here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's where the little cross is?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you can turn to the other side of the railway and indicate again where the water point was where you saw the bodies in the afternoon. Can you tell us that as well.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The water point is here, and I saw the bodies on the other side of this road, by the main road. And the second grave is somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, we'll come to that in a moment, to the second grave. Now, did you, while you were at the water point, did you stay there the whole time or did you go back to where your colleague, Mr. Miladinovic was working?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I went to my colleague. I took him some water. I wasn't by the water point all the time. I was also up there where he was digging. I went to fetch some water for him, and then I went back to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how long did you stay at the water point?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't go to the water point just once. I went maybe two or three times. Sometimes I would stay a bit longer, sometimes a bit shorter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were at that water point, did you see other trucks arriving who would go on to underpass, or didn't that happen?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: When I was there, I believe that it happened once or maybe twice. I can't tell you exactly. I believe that they did pass by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you return to Orahovac that night?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Did you return to Zvornik that night?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: That night we returned to the headquarters of our unit, to the youth settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did that happen? Did somebody pick you up at the water point?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: A vehicle came, a TAM, by the engineering company. The driver was Milutin Bajic. He came. I don't know whether he came to fetch us or was he just passing by and picked us up. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who returned with you to the base?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I and Miladinovic and Risto Lazic as far as I can remember. There may have been one or two other soldiers, but I can't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the time you drove back to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know how long it took us to get there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it already dark?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was already dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back to a last point of clarification, did you have headlights on your G-700?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, I really don't. It should have had headlights, but I don't remember whether it did. I really don't know. It should have headlights. Whether they were in working order or not, I really don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there on that first day, did you see any other large machinery around of your type, your G-700, or any other type? Do you remember that on the first day?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No. We were the only ones there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you returned to the base, did you report to anybody?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do, did you go home to sleep or where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: In the unit, in the base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to the next day. What did you do on the next day?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I got up, had breakfast, followed the normal routine. After breakfast, I waited for my orders to arrive, like every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive orders?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who gave you these orders?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The platoon commander, Damjan Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he order you to do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: He told me to get ready to go to Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he tell you what you were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether he did or whether he didn't. I really can't remember. I just remember that he told me that I was supposed to go to Orahovac to work there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your understanding at that time that you were supposed to do at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: What was I to think? I thought that I would continue digging, what else?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what were your feelings when you were told you had to return to your digging job after all you had seen the night -- the day before?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It was difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why was it difficult?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I had seen all these scenes, dead bodies and so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go alone to Orahovac the next day or did somebody join you?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I think we took the TAM, the TAM took us there, and the platoon commander also went with me and two or three other soldiers. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these soldiers were from which unit?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that they were members of the engineering unit. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember the time you left that morning to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It was before noon, before noon in any case. I can't give you the exact time but I don't remember. I didn't have a watch on me, so I wouldn't be able to give you the exact time. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly did you go to?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: We went to the water point. The TAM left us there. We got off the TAM there, and I went to switch on the engine on my piece of equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the same equipment you had worked with, and your colleague Miladinovic the night -- the day before?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now before we get into what you were doing, can you tell us what you saw at the water point when you arrived that morning.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Not by the water point, but across the road, the road that goes under the pass. I saw bodies and I also saw four or five or maybe six people in civilian clothes wearing overalls or working clothes. And there was some soldiers as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could refer to the sketch, the drawing, you had made, can you tell us where you saw these bodies and these people in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The bodies were here and here, in this area by this thing here. People in the civilian clothes were at the crossroads standing on the road. And the army was also there, the soldiers were there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you just indicated to the area left of what you had described as grave number 2, that crossroad I think a centimetre left of grave number 2. How many people did you see there? You mentioned you saw people in civilian clothes. How many were they?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Those people were wearing overalls or working clothes. There were four or five or six maybe. I didn't count heads, again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what exactly were they doing?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: They were standing there. They were from the civilian protection or from the public utility company from Zvornik. I really don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see what the soldiers were doing?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: They were standing there on the road, by the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned bodies. Can you tell us roughly how many bodies you saw there.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I said that I didn't count them. I didn't pay that much attention, so I can't tell you exactly how many they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. President, that would be a good moment to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ristanovic, you described to us what you saw when you arrived on that second day in Orahovac with your machinery. Now, what were you doing with this machine?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the machine. I switched it on and I returned it under the pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And referring to your drawing, please, where did you drive it to?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I went under the underpass, and there is a meadow on the other side and also at that place there were marks telling me where to dig the second grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the drawing on your left side, on the ELMO, and again use the pointer and tell the Judges where you saw these markings on that meadow. If the usher could assist.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Thereabouts, in this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's just on top of this road, which is on top of the grave number 2, that's where you saw the markings. And did you start digging?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to dig a hole or did something interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't dig the hole. I started digging, and I don't know how much I had dug out. And then the water hose broke and the hose started filling with water, so I couldn't continue digging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I stopped. I did not continue working. I asked somebody what I was supposed to do, and then somebody ordered me to move to a different site, to continue digging there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I crossed to another side and I started digging there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the person that somebody had told you to change locations?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly whether it was the platoon commander or somebody else. I really can't remember who told me to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this second location where you eventually started digging, was that what you had indicated on your sketch as grave number 2?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had described before the break that there were bodies, and I believe it was in that area. Can you clarify again, at that location, grave number 2, did you see bodies?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what area in metres did they cover, these bodies?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I couldn't tell you the surface that they covered. I can't tell you exactly what the surface was. I didn't measure it. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were told to dig a hole, can you tell us the measure of that hole.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Just approximately. I can't give you the precise measurements. It was probably some 10 metres long and the width was the same as -- of the previous hole. It may have been a bit bigger or a bit smaller. I really can't give you the exact measurements, because I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how deep?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Just like the previous one, between a metre and a half and 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you described the size of this hole. Now going back to the bodies you saw, did these bodies cover an area which was bigger or smaller than the grave you were about to dig?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember the size of that surface. I didn't pay too much attention to all that. I didn't have a close look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see other machinery, engineering machinery, present?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything but I heard a machine on the other side. The noise came from the direction of the railroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to tell because somebody told you or because you heard otherwise what machinery that was?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether anybody told me which machine it was. I heard the sound of the machine. Maybe somebody even told me which machine it was. In any case, I could hear it working. I could hear the engine on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what machine it was?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. I suppose it was a loader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this loader, does it have a name?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Every loader has a name, T-200, T-160. They have different names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were digging your grave, did your platoon commander, Lazarevic, come to visit you?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. When you say "platoon commander," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: He was there all the time. He didn't go anywhere. He was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you in fact finish your grave?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at what time in the day were you able to finish it?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It was sometime in the afternoon. I don't know exactly when, but it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do once you had finished digging?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I drove the machine to the main road by the water point; that's where I drove it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did the scenery look like at the water point? Were there still people around, as you had told us earlier?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: There were troops there. There were soldiers there all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that these bodies were transported somewhere, put into the hole you were digging, or didn't that happen while you were there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see when the bodies were put there; it didn't happen while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened next in relation to you and your machinery?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Sometime before dusk, we loaded a machine on to the trailer and returned it to the base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by base, you mean the engineering in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who returned to you -- with you to the base?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The driver, the driver who drove the trailer. I loaded the machine onto his trailer and he was there. Whether there was anybody else sitting with us in that truck, I can't remember, but he must have been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in the base, did you report to anybody?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, no. I unloaded the machine and I really don't remember having reported to anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, within the next couple of days, did you receive another assignment to dig a hole?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I believe that on the following day I didn't go anywhere. As far as I can remember, I didn't go anywhere. So after I returned from that site, on the following day, I didn't go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about the day after that day?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The day after that day, in the morning we got up, we had breakfast. And I believe that a platoon commander, Damjan Lazarevic, came again and he told us to load our equipment and get ready to go to Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the route you took.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: We took the Zvornik/Bijeljina road, and then we took the road that forks off towards Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you loaded your equipment. Was that again the same type of equipment you had used in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you called that, I believe, G-700?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was the loader transported to Branjevo?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean, did you drive yourself to Branjevo with your G-700?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the truck cab with the driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the G-700 in relation to the truck?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: On this Labudica trailer. That is where heavy machinery is placed in order to have the truck pull it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the vehicle that pulled the truck, what type of vehicle that was?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know now what the exact make was. I really can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown, please, exhibit P538. Could you please have a look at the first page, and you see the type Mercedes 2626, and it has a registration number M-5195. And if you can flip to the second page and there is an entry on the 17th of July in handwriting, just third from the bottom. If you can read, please, to the Judges that line starting 17/7/1995.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The 17th of July, 1995, that's what it says. Base, Standard, Branjevo, Baser [phoen]. Then number of rides, 1, 80 kilometres were covered. Transport G-700. That's what is written here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it possible that this was the vehicle, this Mercedes who pulled your machine to Branjevo on that day?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly -- well, it's possible. I mean, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like you to look at the second drawing. I believe you still have it in front of you. That's Exhibit 661. That was the first page of these two drawings. If you can explain to the Judges this drawing. Where did you come from when you arrived at the Branjevo Farm? And I believe the usher is putting -- he has done already the drawing on to the ELMO. Can you, please, take the pointer and explain where you came from.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: We came from Zvornik -- Bijeljina, from the Zvornik/Bijeljina road, which is here. And somewhere around here, the road forks off to Lokanj. That's where Branjevo is, here. I mean in this area, there is a crossroads here. There's this road to Lokanj then Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the end of what the witness said. The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you repeat where you arrived with your trailer.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I said that we were on the Zvornik/Bijeljina road. Before the place called Pilica, there is a road that forks off towards Lokanj. When you take the road to Lokanj, then you continue along that road and that is where Branjevo is. Branjevo is what the locality is called and then we all got there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Branjevo is? This location, what was it used for?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Branjevo is a village, and this other locality was called Ekonomija Branjevo, the Branjevo Farm. I don't know, livestock farm. Well, a farm like a farm. Fruit, like an agricultural cooperative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you refer back to your drawing, you indicated that there are two markings. You marked what appears to be buildings. Can you explain us what buildings those were.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The workshop is there, the workshop of that cooperative, and also there are some auxiliary buildings there, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived, did you see somebody else there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: In front of workshop, I saw a few men, probably the men working there, they were wearing working clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see besides these people -- soldiers?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what were you doing after you had arrived?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: When we got there, I unloaded the machine, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I was told, I think by the platoon commander, that I should take the machine there, and I think it was back there behind the building that we did the digging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to dig a hole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told what size this hole was supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that, whether they said so or not. They probably did, but I don't recall these details, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it about the same size of the graves you had dug the days before in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, around that, perhaps a bit bigger, perhaps a bit smaller, but I don't really remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you again look at your drawing, can you tell us on your drawing where the location of the grave was.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: The grave was -- if viewed from the building, then it was on the right-hand side of the building, so somewhere around here, as far as I can remember. So this is the building, and on the right-hand side, that's where the grave was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived, did you see bodies there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us on your drawing where these bodies were?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Over here, that's where the meadow is, so they were on the meadow. It's like a small valley, and that's where the bodies were. I saw the bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how wide was the area which was covered by these bodies?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean, I really don't know. I really don't know how big it was, the area. I did see the bodies, but I did not walk up to the bodies, and I did not look at it in such detail to see how big an area they covered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to say whether there were more bodies than you had seen in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I did not walk up there. From the place where I was working, it was perhaps about 100 metres away, and I did not walk up at all to see whether there were more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to us whether it was smelling.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say yes or no, because where I worked there was also a barn and there was the smell of fertiliser. Now, whether this smell also came or not, I really cannot remember that detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you didn't go to see the bodies. Why didn't you go?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't go because I already felt sick having seen all these bodies, what I saw in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from your engineering equipment, was there another machinery there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, later on a loader arrived and went towards the corpses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to be shown the next exhibit. This is Exhibit number 5, but before I show you that, can you describe the loader to us, please.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, four wheels and in front there was this big grab, this thing that is used for loading, whatever people call it, and in front there is the cab for the driver and that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's Exhibit number 63. Do you remember the colour of that machinery?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: For the most part, these loaders are yellow. For the most part, those that I saw. Yellow, I think that's what it would be called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember the brand of the machine?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know it's a loader, but I don't know the exact type. I did not walk up to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could show him Exhibit Number 63. If you can have a look at it. Is the loader you saw on that day similar to this one?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did this machinery do on that day?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw it there. I saw it arrive there, but I did not see specifically what it did there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "there," where do you mean? If you can go back to your drawing and tell us the location where you saw that loader working.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, over here, this is where the corpses were, in this area around here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the loader was in the middle of the corpses; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Next to it. It's a big meadow, so it was somewhere nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was it doing?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: While I was working, while I was digging, it just stood there. It didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see later what it was doing?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No. When I finished digging, I returned the machine to the road, and I went to the first houses that are there to get water. And I sat there by the road, on the other side, and I could not see at all what the loader was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you return to the base on that day again?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember the time you left the Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon I think. I know for sure that we returned before it got dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did return with you, if anybody?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I only know the driver who drove the truck. Now, whether there was anybody else sitting in the cab with us, I really can't remember that detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take your machinery, your G-700, with you or did it stay there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: We loaded it on the Labudica and returned it to the base of the engineering company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you hear or did somebody tell you what happened to these graves you had dug in Orahovac and in Branjevo?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to show you a number of vehicle logs of the Zvornik Brigade in relation to engineering vehicles. And I would like to start with Exhibit 515. And in fact, I do have the original with me which can be shown to the Defence, perhaps first, and also to the Judges. It's the original of 515. And perhaps a copy can be placed onto the ELMO. Now, this appears to be the vehicle log for a backhoe excavator. And in your language, B/C/S, it says Rovokopac, and it has a registration number C-3117. And looking at it, you also see that the head of the first page is typewritten, the type of the machine and also the registration number and your name and another name appears there typewritten as well. Now, there are handwriting entries on that page and also on the next page, if you can flip over to the next page. If the B/C/S version could be placed on to the ELMO. Now, let me ask you to read what it says on the second page on entry 14/07. Can you read that out, please.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is what it says: For whose needs does it work, the VRS it says. The road covered. The base, Orahovac, and the way back. The actual work: Digging trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what this machine was, this backhoe excavator, or Rovokopac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a type of backhoe excavator. Some people call it Rovokopac, some people call it Skip, it depends on what people call it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, the 14th of July, did you use this machine?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who made these handwriting -- handwritten entries in this document on both sides of this page?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us an explanation why your name appears here on this worksheet, giving dates you were working with this machinery, apparently. Can you give us an explanation for that, if you have any.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN RISTANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to explain this to you. According to the establishment of the unit and according to who the machines were issued to, I was assigned to this machine, and this Milos Mitrovic.
